title: Muscle mechanical characteristics in fatigue and recovery from a marathon race in highly trained runners
authors: Petersen K, Hansen CB, Aagaard P, Madsen K
population: 8 elite marathon runners (2:34:40 +/- 0:04:13), tested 1 week before and 30 min, 2 and 5 days after
findings: Energy expenditure at marathon pace rose 4% post-marathon (4,465 +/- 91 to 4,638 +/- 91 J/kg/km, P < 0.05) but was 6% and 9.5% lower two and five days post-marathon than pre-marathon.
Countermovement jump power fell 13% post-marathon (21.5 to 18.9 W/kg) and remained depressed at two (18%) and five (12%) days; CMJ force was unaltered.
Knee extensor MVC fell from 176.6 to 136.7 Nm (22%) and plantar flexor MVC from 144.9 to 119.2 Nm (17%) post-marathon.

No significant change in evoked contractile properties except a 25% increase in force at 5 Hz, and low frequency fatigue was not observed; authors infer central rather than peripheral mechanisms and that leg muscle power recovered very slowly.
limitations: n = 8 elite runners; no testing beyond day 5; the later drop in energy expenditure at marathon pace is as reported and not explained as readiness; findings may not generalise to recreational runners.
implications: Jump power is still about 12% down on day 5 after a marathon in well-trained runners, so a return that adds speed, strides or plyometrics inside the first week after a marathon is not supported; keep the first week easy and low-impact.
Do not read the later drop in energy cost as readiness: the abstract does not interpret it as such and the sample is 8.

verification.notes: Crossref (2007-07-28, authors match) and abstract re-read (PMID 17661071); all numbers match. Added CMJ force unaltered and low-frequency-fatigue-not-observed to findings.
